utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Registrar, would you please have our witness brought in? (The accused/witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good morning to the interpreters. I hope that everybody is feeling fine today. It is Friday. Good morning to the Prosecution and to the Defence and good morning to the accused, who is our witness. Having said this, I think, Mr. Nobilo, that we can continue with the detailed examination-in-chief relating to the day of 16 April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. For orientation of the Trial Chamber, there are three dramatic days: the 16th, 17th, and 18th. We will try to provide a minute-by-minute reconstruction of those three days, and then after we leave April, we will just focus on particular issues and how they were resolved. I would like to go into very minute detail as to what happened during those three crucial days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yesterday we left at 11.05, so now at 11.15, an attempt was made to establish communication with the main staff. Who tried to do this?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I tried to establish contact with the main headquarters and inform them of the developing events and request that they mediate to achieve a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 11.15, you received the first news of the death -- the first death of a commander in the area; do you recall this? If not ... From Donji Veceriska, one of the commanders called you, that is, one of the members of the Operative Zone command called you. Who was it, why wasn't he at the command post, and what was going on over there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He could not --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: His name was Mile Vinac. He could not reach the command post from Donji Veceriska, but he made a telephone call and reported that it was very critical --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. I would like to share what we just mentioned, my colleagues and I. I am saying this to the Defence. When you point out a fact, I do understand that you do it minute by minute, but there has to be a certain consistency to it. Let me give you an example. At 11.15, the witness, that is, the accused in this case, said that he got in touch with the general staff. Now, in order to gain some time, we have to know what the answer to that was; otherwise, we're going to ask it at one point, what did they tell him at headquarters, because it is important to know that the accused called to the headquarters, but I think what's even more important is to know what he was told. We are at the very root now of the chain of command. I wanted to say this to you so that we would later avoid other problems, and then during the cross-examination, things will go more easily and more efficiently as well. If you agree. If you prefer not to do that, I really don't care.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We agree, and we invite Your Honours to jump in and note points of interest, because I think Mr. Nobilo may indeed be trying to go too fast. These are very important events, and as the Court may observe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: -- I am constantly advising him to slow down so that these matters can be absorbed, and I would encourage him to pose that question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: May I add one little word? As the President has said and you would have observed, members of the Bench have not been intervening in the course of the testimony of the witness. This is because we appreciate that there is a need for you to adhere to a programme concerning the production of evidence. But in the case of this witness, who is a particular witness and whose testimony is expected to be of a certain duration and importance, individual members of the Bench would occasionally be throwing out questions for clarification purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification, Judge Shahabuddeen. We don't like to interrupt, but there are points that we do like to indicate to you. But, of course, you are the one controlling your own strategy, and you should conduct your strategy the way you see fit. Mr. Hayman, do you want to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: This presentation is for an audience of three, Your Honours. You are the audience. Judge Shahabuddeen is absolutely right. In a month or five weeks of testimony, to keep a question in your mind and ask it in three weeks is almost Herculean. Even with a laptop computer, it is difficult to keep track of such information. So we really do invite and ask you to participate actively in the examination, both during the direct and the cross-examination. Please do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. As for Mr. Nobilo, he has to understand that not only are the Judges supervising and watching what he's doing but his colleague is doing the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In any event, I am sort of torn between the need to speed the whole process along and to provide as much detail as possible. So let me second what my colleague has just said. We would appreciate if the Judges ask additional questions. I think we would not lose any quality; on the contrary, we would gain. Let me point out about this detail: The witness may have a very short note about this particular event. Then, if he only has just this short note, he will say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So let me just confirm with you: After you called the main headquarters, what did they tell you, if you recall it at all, what they told you when you asked them to mediate in achieving a cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I called them at 11.15, they only said that they would mediate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let's now go to 11.20 hours. You received a call from the member of the command. Who was this?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was Mr. Mile Vinac, and the call was a telephone call which came from Donji Veceriska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was his position? Where did he work?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He worked at the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command. He was a staff member. He was one of the officers, that is, one of the assistants.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What did he report to you about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He reported that they had been attacked and that they did not have enough ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 11.25, the military intelligence service, the VOS, V-O-S, which was monitoring communications, intercepted a communication which was coming from Stari Vitez. What was that information?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I received information from Old Vitez that they had not received the signal which was supposed to have reached them at 0400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did Sefkija Dzidic also say something about the possibility of withdrawal from Old Vitez, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I do not recall this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 11.40, you had another contact with Kordic. What was that contact about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was a new contact with Kordic, and it was an update about the operations and the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you report to Kordic, or was it an exchange of information?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I gave him information.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 11.42, Pasko Ljubicic called for the first time. What information did he give you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Pasko said, at 11.42, "We are fighting. It is tough. They are resilient. They are throwing at us everything that they have. They are even using women. The most critical and the toughest situation is around the school building, around the mosque, and in individual homes."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you understand from this conversation where Pasko was located and where the fighting was going on?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that Pasko called me on the telephone, and I assumed that he could have been calling from the Bungalow.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That is where he picked up the phone and called you from. But where his military police units were at the time, when you said he told you it's very tough?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I concluded from this report that he was in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 11.47, you had contact with the artillery. Who initiated this contact?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This contact concerned the drafting or compiling a plan for artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 11.50, again relating to the artillery fire, you had a conversation with Cerkez, commander of the Vitez unit.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Cerkez was seeking artillery support against the BH army positions at Kruscica, and he informed me about the fire from Kruscica, Vranjska, Pezici, and Rovna.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you show on this model what was that front line which was being established, Kruscica, Pezici, Vranjska, and Rovna?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am pointing. Vitez, Kruscica, Vranjska, Pezici, Rovna (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was this a line south of the road which you had anticipated in your previous orders as probably being the line of battle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, just a second. I was switched to the French channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That's not a problem. That's not a failure there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's my fault, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We'll try to fix the problem.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I understood the question. I heard it on the proper channel now. Yes, this is the line that was being established between Rovna, Pezici, Vranjska, and Kruscica (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was this the line which you anticipated in your orders?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 11.55, the order was issued to open fire. Who issued it and what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was following the request of Commander Cerkez. I issued it, and fire was opened by the combined artillery battery against the targets which were requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 11.55, you released information for the public. What did it contain?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It only -- it is hard for me to now give you the exact contents of this report, but it just provided information about the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, I know, after six years, it's difficult. But what were you trying to achieve with this release of information?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We just wanted to inform the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How did you describe this? What did you say, who attacked whom?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The press release said that we had been attacked by the BH army early that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you remember some of the addressees of this report?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that it was sent to the UN representatives, to the European Monitoring Mission, to the address of the 3rd Corps, and to our associates.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you mean, your associates?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: To our subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How about the media?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know what media, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I do not recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 12.07, Cerkez gave you information about the situation on the ground, including several villages. Could you tell what locations were included in that information and what type of information was it? What did it contain?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I remember that Mario informed me that we had a critical situation in Donji Veceriska, that there was intense fighting in the area of Kruscica, Gradina, and Kruscica, Sivrino Brdce, and that the Vitez Brigade did not have a link with the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade in Donja Rovna. In other words, there was no contact between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: From this report where your attention was drawn to the flash points, in other words, when you received such a report, does that mean that you, as a commander, then direct your attention and your activities towards the locations which are at most risk? Is that your usual method of work?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Cerkez said that the situation was very critical in this area, and I would like to mention also that he informed me that the situation was very uncertain in Poculica, so I focused my attention to these locations which were pointed to me by Commander Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When the brigade commander says that the brigade is not linked up, what does it mean, to have a link or to be linked up?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That meant that there was no physical or optical or visual contact or any other contact between the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade and the Vitez Brigade in Donja Rovna. In other words, the situation was completely unclear. So it could have meant that there was a breakthrough there, but the situation in the area, who controlled the area, and what the situation was in that area was unknown to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 12.10 hours, you called Grubesic, commander of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade. Could you tell us what prompted you to call him, and what instructions or what orders did you give him?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I called Grubesic because when I received information from Cerkez that the situation was critical at several of his positions and that he had no contact in Donja Rovna, I asked Grubesic to attempt to establish contact with Cerkez in Donja Rovna, and I asked him to defend Kula, Kuber, and Prosje features to the last.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What type of defence did you order at Kuber? What type of defence is it and why?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I ordered that we defend Kuber to the last, which meant that regardless of any withdrawal or any movements towards the main highway, Zenica-Vitez, this feature was not to be relinquished, abandoned, because the defence of these positions was an issue of our survival. Kula was also vital for Busovaca, but Kuber was vital for the entire area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 12.15, you received two calls regarding monitoring, and you received it from MTD.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I received a call from the MTD officer, and I asked him to speed up the process of deploying his spotters, and I asked that any information should be sent back to me, that is, wherever there was any shelling, any artillery activity, we wanted to identify the points of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you received this information about spotting, did you pay attention to the precision of artillery fire, and how did you go about the use of artillery, of the howitzers and guns?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of course, we paid attention about the proper spotting, and we tried to gather information from the spotters in the field, that is, from the units which were supported by artillery but also from the spotters who were members of the artillery batteries. We then tried to compare the data, do proper corrections, and then proceed with fire based on this information. This is how we operated, but it was a time-consuming process. Sometimes it took hours. We targeted certain military targets based on the requests of certain commanders, and these were usually features, strategic features, where the BH army units were deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Later on, we will see in this chronology that you had a lot of contacts with the artillery and that corrections were done and a lot of information was exchanged that way. Can we draw a conclusion that you were trying to be selective and accurate? In other words, if you just shell something randomly, what would be the use of the artillery in that sense?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If you just shelled randomly, the commander would call me or the artillery commander and ask for support without spotting or without taking into account all security measures which were due in such cases, and this would mean that you could respond with artillery fire immediately upon request.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 12.20, you received information from Cerkez that Radio Sarajevo did not broadcast anything. What was that about? What was Radio Sarajevo supposed to broadcast?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that they should have broadcast a statement for the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 12.25, there were new negotiations in Nova Bila. Who went to these negotiations, with whom, and what was that about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were negotiations that were initiated in the course of the morning by the UNPROFOR command, and the deputy head of the joint commission, Mr. Marko Prskalo, went to attend the meeting and Mr. Zoran Pilicic, and the meeting was to have been with the representatives of the 3rd Corps at the UN base in Nova Bila. I gave instructions to Mr. Marko Prskalo to discuss a cease-fire, a cessation of hostilities and all combat operations and the immediate cessation of shelling and that the terrain be cleared up and that information be sought as to the missing officers from the Zenica Brigade and the Novi Travnik Brigade and the prisoners from the Frankopan Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When Prskalo, at 12.25, left, and at 12.25, you were worried about the ammunition situation, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had been worried about this situation for quite some time because we did not have any logistics supplies for a long time, and I tried to find ways and means of having assistance in ammunition, having more ammunition and supplies, particularly for the Vitez unit where this lack of ammunition was a crucial point, and I also asked that the logistics base in Stojkovici monitor the ammunition situation and check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 12.27, the civilian police and the chief of the civilian police contacted you. What happened there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The civilian police established contact, and there were two issues that were discussed: One was the question of sniper action from Stari Vitez and from Sljibcice from the positions of the BH army, and the second issue discussed was the roads which could be used in communication towards the hospital in Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you tell us, if you remember, who you talked to at 12.27 and 12.30 from the ranks of the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I talked to Mr. Mirko Samija. He was the chief of the police station in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us whether he gave you information as to the situation in the town itself, and, if so, what was that information?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He did give me information on the fact that, in town, there were numerous calls being made and that the situation in town, the security situation, was very difficult and precarious because there was sniper fire from all positions in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. Samija, did he say from which positions there was sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He said from the position of Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 12.34, you talked to the commander of the Tvrtko to be placed at the disposal of the Vitez Brigade. What was that agreement about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That agreement came after a request made by the commander of the Vitez Brigade to be given backup in Donja Veceriska, and I asked the commander of Tvrtko to see to extending assistance to the defenders of Donja Veceriska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 12.36, Kordic called you once again. Why?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Kordic called again because of what was going on at Kuber and the unfavourable situation, and he asked me to give him information as to what was actually going on in that region from the direction of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 12.42, you called Pasko Ljubicic by phone, and what was the motive for that telephone call? What did you ask him to do and what did he tell you? What information did he give you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to consult my colleagues on a point. You can continue, Mr. Nobilo. Excuse me. We had to speak for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No problem. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You had a telephone conversation with Pasko at 12.42. Did you receive any fresh information?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I asked for information from Pasko, and I received a report that he was holding his positions and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The term "to hold his positions," what does that tell you as a military man? What does that mean to you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It meant that he and his men were immobile, static, and that probably a front line had been established.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 12.45, you gave an order for ammunition to be sent. Who did you send ammunition to?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I sent ammunition to the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 12.50, once again Cerkez phoned. What was that about this time?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Cerkez phoned again with respect to Donja Veceriska and the situation in Donja Veceriska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did he ask anything of you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He asked for help in the form of men for Donja Veceriska, and I told him that we were already working on sending backup and that they should hold on for a little while longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 12.52, from Tomislavgrad, a member of the command phoned you. What was that about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From Tomislavgrad, the head of the engineers phoned and informed me that he was blocked and that he was not able to call in to report to the Vitez command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.02, you once again worked with the commander of the artillery and Cerkez. What was that about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was once again a request for backup, for support to forces, but now at the Kuber feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.10, Cerkez informed you about the situation. Do you remember what he said on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He conveyed information to me that all the Croats in Poculica had been completely encircled and that there were wounded and that they were not able to evacuate the wounded. I told him that we would seek the engagement of UNPROFOR so that UNPROFOR, with its vehicles, could evacuate the injured from Poculica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.12, you informed the main staff. What information did you give the main staff?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I sent out information on the situation and the number of killed, the figures that we had collected up until then. There were 15 killed soldiers according to the reports we had received by 13.12.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.15, you had talks with Stjepan Siber. Could you tell us who he was and what you discussed with him?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Stjepan Siber was the deputy chief of staff of the supreme command or army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I also discussed with him a cease-fire, a cessation to the fighting, and I asked that he act as a go-between and mediate with the 3rd Corps in Zenica so as to ensure an immediate cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.20, once again a member of the command, Mile Vinac, called. Where was he calling from, what did he want, and what was his conduct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He said in a panic-stricken voice and through tears that he was calling from his home in Donja Veceriska. He said that they could not leave the house, that he had been left without any ammunition, and he kept repeating, "It's over. We're finished. We're finished." I tried to calm him, and I told him to hold out for a little while longer because help was on its way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was he at a combat position with his wife and children?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He phoned me, and he said he was telephoning from his family house where he lived with his wife and his children and the other members of his family. I think his mother or his father lived with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you explain the emotional state that he was in?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it was the voice of a desperate man, of a man who was lost. He cried. He said what he said through tears while he was asking for my help. There was a feeling that he was absolutely -- he felt there was no hope and that he didn't know how he was going to live. He kept repeating, "We're finished. We're finished. This is the end."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.20, that is to say, right after that conversation, you checked to see whether help had arrived; is that true? Who was to send that aid and who was the aid being sent to?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The aid and assistance was to be sent to the Vitez Brigade towards Donja Veceriska, and I asked that checks be made with the commander of the Tvrtko unit, and the information I received was that help was on its way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.22, you called UNPROFOR, the UN Why?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I called UNPROFOR asking for their help for civilians in the village of Poculica. There were two of them stranded there. The duty officer answered. I don't know his name. At that point, I was told that they declined to provide assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.25, feature 916 was shelled. What was the significance of this feature and what was it shelled with?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That feature was at Kuber and, in fact, it was a position and it was shelled in order to slow down the advance from Kuber to Vrana Stijene and Obla Glava.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was it shelled with?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: With a howitzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It was not clear who was shelling. Which side?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it by your orders?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.26, you had another contact with Cerkez. Why did you contact him then?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It again concerned the situation in Donja Veceriska where he again asked that assistance be sent as soon as possible, and I asked him to wait a little bit longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Again, you talked to MTD regarding the targets in Poculica.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that was a contact regarding targeting the feature, I think, 592 at Sljibcice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was there at Sljibcice?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to our information, there was an anti-aircraft gun stationed there and BH army units which were in combat positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.32, you received a call from the main headquarters of the BH army. Do you recall that call?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, we received a call from -- I think that one of my associates received this call from the main headquarters of the BH army in Sarajevo, and we were told that they are agreeing to a cessation of operations and that Dzemo Merdan would arrive in Vitez with a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.35, you tried to reach Filipovic. Why?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I wanted to confirm whether Filipovic had established contact with Commander Alagic in Travnik and whether he had established what the movements of the 17th Krajina Brigade in Travnik were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you succeed in establishing contact?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I established contact with Filipovic, but he had not yet established contact with Alagic by that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.36, Slavko Marin called Cerkez and transmitted a message to him. What was that contact about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That contact was about the announced cessation of operations between the HVO and the BH army, and it was just really transmitting the message we had just previously received from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.39, you received another call from Donja Veceriska?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The situation was identical to the one previously. Again, Vinac called sobbing, saying that the help was not there yet and that it was the end of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So did he sort of try to say good-bye?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he said something to the effect that he wanted to say good-bye and he said that they were close and this would be the last time that we spoke. He said, "The houses are burning around me. They will probably kill us all."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.44, Kordic called again to transmit to you information which you received from the BH army.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was the information about the announced, as I said, announced cessation of fire between the HVO and the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you inform him of the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I told him that the most critical situation was at Poculica and Donja Veceriska, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.48, you spoke to Grubesic. What did he ask of you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Grubesic informed me that the positions at Kuber which they had held were lost and that he could not see a way to stay at Kuber, and taking into account the situation of Croats in Poculica who were completely surrounded, I asked him to stay at Kuber at any cost and to try to establish contact with members of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 13.52, Pasko Ljubicic called. Can you say what he reported about and what instructions you gave him?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He told me that they were still holding their positions, and I asked him to take into account that the crucial point was, and I quote, "Hold on up there," meaning the slope above Ahmici and Nadioci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you tell me, what did you order him? What did you see as most important in his sector of activity? What was the crucial point for him to do? I think this is a significant point. Perhaps, if you need to, you can remove some of these red pylons so we can see. First of all, based on what you understood from Pasko Ljubicic's report, where was he? First of all, where did he dig in?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to the reports I received, this was right here (indicating). It was in front of the mosque and the school. The front line, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: According to your information then, where was fighting going on?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That location was in front of the school and mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where are the school and mosque in the village in relation to the road? Above the road? Below the road? How far from the road are they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They are north, that is, above the road, up to 150 metres at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So they were still in the area of the road. What did you ask of them? What was to be their task?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I asked them to take the slope, that is, Vidovici, Barin Gaj, and farther on to Kratine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In terms of the ground, would that be high ground or low ground?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: High ground exclusively because the road had already been cut off. So to hold the high ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why was it important to hold the hill? Why is it wrong, in military terms, to be on the road in the village?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is important to hold the high ground, that is, a hill, because only in that way can you control the road for traffic, and the position in the village has absolutely no military significance.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: As a soldier, what did you consider important? That the military be in the village or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, the village had no significance. For me, the most important thing was that we hold this high ground, Kratine -- hold on a second -- Barin Gaj, and to establish a line on that position, which would also be defended to the last in order to prevent a link-up and to secure the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In military terms, how is a road defended? Do you stand on the road, on the pavement, or do you need to hold certain other points, locations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: A road can only be defended if you control the high ground and positions and features around it. This is very clear on this model because whoever controls the high ground and features absolutely controls the communication line and traffic, because at any time, with the artillery and with fire, he can cut off the road and prevent traffic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would it have been extremely dangerous for you had the BH army taken the Barin Gaj slope?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was the only slope remaining at Kuber after the BH army had taken it and, of course, it posed the highest risk for the entire Operative Zone and for me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you, at 13.52, told Pasko, "You have to take that thing up there, this thing up here," what did you mean by "this thing up here"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I meant Barin Gaj and the slope between Vidovici Kuce and above Nadioci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does that mean that you basically are forcing him out of the village and uphill?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I asked of him, out of the village, and I told him that he had to take this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may go back to your seat now. At 13.55, Cerkez called again. What did he tell you? What did you tell him?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Cerkez called again, and again these calls now kept pouring in from Poculica, Donja Veceriska, and from the area of Kruscica. So he informed me about the developments in that area, and he said that the critical situation continued to be in Donja Veceriska and that he had a problem with wounded in Poculica. I told him that they should hold out a while longer and that I had requested assistance from the UN forces to evacuate the wounded from Poculica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If we were to sum up these reports from the early morning up to that point by Cerkez, what was the situation like? Was it going well or was it unfavourable?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He said that the situation was especially difficult in Donja Veceriska and Poculica at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 14.00 hours, after a previous failed attempt, you reached Mirko Samija. What was that conversation about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was trying to -- first of all, he is the chief of the police station of the Vitez civilian police force, and the information that I was seeking was the condition of the roads in the town of Vitez with respect to snipers. I asked him whether there were any alternate roads to the hospital in Nova Bila. He informed me that from Stari Vitez, Old Vitez, and Sljibcice, all roads leading to the hospital in Nova Bila were controlled and that we were unable to evacuate the wounded to Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who controlled these roads?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was controlled by the BH army through snipers and through fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 14.05, you unsuccessfully tried to reach Kraljevic. Why were you trying to reach him? Had he been calling up until that point?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I kept trying to reach him on the telephone. I was trying, but I still could not reach him at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, during that battle on the 16th, he had been attached to you in that moment, and you described what that means. He was subordinate to you at that moment. Can you tell me, was it usual that the superior officer is trying to reach a subordinate officer, or would it have been appropriate that the subordinate officer is trying to reach the superior?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It would have been appropriate that he called me, so I was concerned that Kraljevic was not reporting. I wanted to know what was going on with him and his men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 14.07, you again issued an order to the artillery?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did issue an order for artillery support upon request.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 14.08, you had another conversation with the chief of police. What was that conversation concerning?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It had to do with the security situation in the town of Vitez, and we also discussed ways of protecting ourselves from snipers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next, Dzemo Merdan called again.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was a call from the 3rd Corps, it was received by Slavko Marin --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Excuse me. My question was -- I didn't say that Dzemo Merdan called again, no, but that he finally called for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is that correct, that he called at that point for the first time?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He called regarding the calming of the situation, and we also asked that the fighting cease.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you agree on anything further?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I do not recall any further details.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 14.20, Pilicic and Prskalo returned from negotiations. What information did you get from them? Who was present there and how did the negotiations proceed?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Marko Prskalo first told me that no one from the 3rd Corps command was present, that is, from the BH army group in Zenica, and the negotiations were between the members of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command and representatives of Sefkija, who was a member of the municipal staff in Vitez, and either the chief of staff of -- the deputy commander of the 325th Brigade of the BH army. It was Mr. Sivro, at any rate. Marko told me that the cease-fire had been agreed, that separation of forces was also agreed, release of all detained and captured individuals, care for the wounded, patrolling of the UN forces, and that a new meeting was called for 17th April at 9.00 at the UN base. Marko also told me that on the way back from the UN base, the UNPROFOR base, towards the Hotel Vitez, he saw a body of a civilian lying next to the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, it's a long morning. We suggest a 15-minute break, and then we will resume from 10.30 until 11.45, and the second break will be 30 minutes. Would that be all right for the interpreters? Very well. All right. We will suspend the hearing the until 10.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now resume the hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We left off with the return of Prskalo and Pilicic from the negotiations, and they told you that they had seen civilian bodies lying by the roadside, that is, the body of one civilian lying by the road. Did they tell you whether there was any mention at the meeting about any civilian casualties?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They did not inform me at the meeting. The meeting had discussed civilians but they just informed me of the items on the agenda and what I already stated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the basis of the oral agreement that they reached on your behalf, did you issue any orders following that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I issued an order, and the registration number was 01-4-271/93, dated the 16th of April, 1993. The order was to implement the agreement that had been reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mean the cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 14.30, you once again had a talk with Kordic. What did you inform him of?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I informed him of Dzemo's call from the command of the 3rd Corps and the offer regarding a cease-fire and the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At 14.32, Nakic called you. He was your chief of staff. Tell us what you talked about.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He also informed me that he was blocked and that there was still fighting around his village, and he conveyed to me that he had talked to Dzemo Merdan and that they had discussed a cessation of hostilities. I also informed Nakic and he informed me, I asked him whether he had received any new information about Totic and the officers that had been kidnapped from the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade from Novi Travnik, and I conveyed, that is to say, Nakic told me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is there a problem with the interpretation, Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No, we're just trying quickly to find a document, a Defence Exhibit, to show you, so Mr. Hayman was making secret signs with our clerk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What did Dzemo tell you? What else? Did you inform him of the situation you found yourself in?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The chief of staff, Nakic, I informed him about the situation, and I told him that we had 15 dead but that we were still holding out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You referred to one of your orders, 01-4-271/93, it was Defence Exhibit D279, and so the secret negotiation that was going on was not very precise. We're going to repeat this then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, you're only responding to instructions from the Judges. That's very good and congratulations. Did you find the document? We have it now. General Blaskic, this is the order of 16 April. This is 01-4-271/93. Would you like to make a comment about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mentioned the registration number, and we remembered that we had the order and that it was Defence Exhibit D279, dated the 16th of April, 1993, the time is 16.00 hours, and you were ordering in point 1: "All units in your zone of responsibility are to be immediately ordered to discontinue and cease all combat actions against Muslim forces." You sent this order to the Vitez Brigade and to the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade. We're not going to read the whole order, but we should just like to clarify certain points. You sent this to the commanders of the two brigades, and you say, "All units in your zone of responsibility are to be immediately ordered to discontinue and cease all combat actions ..." What does that mean? Who did this refer to?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It referred to all units which were engaged in the zone of Vitez and the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade area or, if we look at it in terms of space, it means all units of the Busovaca municipality and the Vitez municipality which were engaged in combat action.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In concrete terms, the Tvrtkovci, the military police, and the Vitezovi, and now looking at it from military terminology, in whose zone of combat action or zone of responsibility were they active?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They functioned in the zone of responsibility of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Therefore, when you, in point 1 of your order, order Cerkez and Grubesic from the Vitez --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. I think, Mr. President, I have sat for awhile, as we have sat while Mr. Nobilo testifies in part, and, with all due respect, I would ask, Mr. President, to allow Mr. Nobilo to ask a question and then allow the witness to say what he means by certain things and certain times, as opposed to counsel leading him along that path, if you will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, do you have an answer to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am trying to do that. I am trying to get the witness's views as to what he thinks, and I think he concluded what he was saying when I started my question. That was the impression that I gained, at any rate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The alternative, and we can do it, is that for every point, Mr. Nobilo will need to ask, "At 14.20 hours, did you have a contact with someone? With whom did you have a contact? Did you contact him or did he contact you? What was said?" Next point, "At 14.25, did you have a contact," so there will be three or four questions just to establish the point in time and who is speaking. We can do that, but it will double the length of the examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There is an easy solution to that and that takes place in many courts, Mr. President, and that is "When was your next contact and what happened?" I don't think that's a particularly difficult endeavour to undertake. The difficulty, Mr. President, and I don't mean to interrupt counsel's presentation here, is that over the past seven days, and obviously counsel thinks this is extremely important, there would appear to be a direction in the methodology of questioning that I think is something less than spontaneous for the witness, and I simply ask that counsel ask the witness an open question and allow the witness to provide the details, as opposed to the other way around. That's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. This is a very relevant issue, and it is of concern to us. I would like to consult with my colleagues about it. The Judges have thought about this very important question, and this is their decision and the reasons for the decision: First of all, it is true, Mr. Nobilo, that the Defence witness has not been testifying spontaneously as of today, and the Judges would like him to testify spontaneously, all the more so because this is not a witness like other witnesses but rather one who is in contact with you on a permanent basis. Therefore, in order to ensure the equilibrium of these proceedings, the Defence counsel has a whole log of things that he wants to have said, and he simply has to ask the questions so that the witness can answer, and the Judges would like the testimony to be spontaneous and free. The Judges have decided as follows: We are going to ask the accused to testify freely in large chunks. In other words, "General Blaskic, what happened on the afternoon of the 16th of April," and then, Mr. Nobilo, you can ask all the questions that you feel are necessary to specify certain points which were not specified in the testimony and which you want to have specified by the witness. Of course, he's going to have gaps in his memory, things he just does not remember, but you can put him back on the right track, you can, if necessary, interrupt him, but the Judges do not want any longer to have you start with a very specific background, a very specific plan that you have in mind. The Judges do no longer want to have the witness being guided in such a way that he's no longer testifying spontaneously. In all legal systems, a witness has to testify spontaneously, and that is why in all legal systems there is a prohibition against witnesses making written testimony because that distorts the proceedings. We're now speaking about the 16th of April in the afternoon, and the Judges turn to the witness and ask him what happened on that afternoon, and then you, Mr. Nobilo, and no one is going to count your time, you will specify certain points but being very careful that you're asking questions, this is a very important point, and that you are not moving along through affirmations. Have I been clear? Mr. Hayman, would you like to make a comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We will do as you request, but we object that you are prohibiting Defence counsel from putting specific questions to our client, and we think that is undue interference in the method of examination of the accused. We should be allowed to direct the witness's attention to specific events and points in time, but we will proceed. I simply want to preserve the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, you're a very skilful attorney, but I'm also a skilful Judge. I understand what you're saying, thinking about the future of the proceedings, but we have Rules and we have the power to question the witness as we like at any point that we want to question him, and I want this to be in the transcript: I have just said that the Defence will ask any specific questions it wishes to ask, but it should be noted, we are not trying to, in any way, prejudice the accused's rights, but we do not want, and this is a fundamental point in all legal systems, that is, a testimony -- this is not the case which might be remote-controlled which means that "At 14.00 hours you did this, General Blaskic," and then General Blaskic, says, "Yes, at 14.00 hours, I did do this." That's Mr. Nobilo testifying, no longer General Blaskic, and this is why I'm responding to your objection, Mr. Hayman. If we follow all Rules, and we're all reading the same Rules, I'm sure that we would come to a meeting point in our interpretation of the text. Having said this clearly and having this marked clearly in the record, we are not, in any way, trying to have the witness not say what he wants to say but rather that he should say what he wants to say freely and spontaneously. He is the main player in all of this, first of all, because he is the accused and because he lived through all of the facts minute by minute, and, of course, at any point, including a moment when you want to interrupt him, you can ask questions, but I want you to ask questions and not to proceed through affirmations and assertions. That's what the Judges want, if you look at the texts that are in force here at the Tribunal and to be sure that they are being properly interpreted, and, of course, this corresponds to all practices in all developed legal systems. Having said this, Mr. Nobilo, we are now at the point where you can resume the examination-in-chief, calling your witness's attention to the fact that he has to tell us about what happened during the day of 16 April. Mr. Nobilo, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Of course, we can do this. We can ask the questions in different ways. However, I would like to point out that within the last ten days, by this method, I edited out about 60 to 70 per cent of all the facts that I believe that General Blaskic would have otherwise testified to. General Blaskic keeps a wealth of details in his mind, and I just wanted to make sure that we came to the most essential ones but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, I understand what you're saying very clearly, and you know the Judges do not want to waste any time. It is self-evident that if the accused, who is now a witness, were to get lost in too many details or have trouble remembering certain points, you would be there to help him, and I suppose that with the contacts that you've had with your client for the past 20 months, you should know what seems to be essential for his defence and what's less essential. This is your mission, this is your assignment, and this is your monopoly, if you like. If you agree, we will now continue speaking about the afternoon of the 16th of April, but we will stop making affirmations, after which the witness will simply say, "Yes" or "No," "I did this" or "I did that." I repeat, it is not the Defence who is testifying but, rather, the accused, General Blaskic, and we are fully cognisant of his rights and we are protecting them. Mr. Nobilo, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Let me just go back to Exhibit D279 because I don't think we have finished and it is significant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General Blaskic, can you explain what point 1 means, when you say "in all areas of your zone of responsibility"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Point 1 reads: "All units in your zone of responsibility are to be IMMEDIATELY ordered to discontinue and cease all combat actions ..." By that I meant the zone of responsibility of the commanders of the Vitez Brigade and Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade. In the heading, I said that it was to be delivered directly to both of these two commanders, and point 1 implied all units which were operating in the zone of responsibility of either of those two brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did this also refer to the special purpose units and the military police units?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let's go back to the sequence of events. What went on from 14.36 April 16th and onward?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 14.36, we had correction of the artillery fire and had communication with the commander of the artillery battery and Mr. Slavko Marin talked to him. Also, at around 14.40 hours, I inquired about the situation in Travnik, and I talked to the brigade commander from Novi Travnik, and after that, after this conversation, I was informed that Officer Lastro from Travnik was unable to report to the command post because he could not use the roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before we move to the chronology with respect to this order, what was the reason for your issuing such an order after about half a day of fighting?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My motivation from the early morning of 16 April was to stabilise the situation and effect a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. Obviously we are referring to Exhibit 279.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the basis of everything you have just said, were you able to push back the BH army forces at any of the points?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. We were the side which was being pushed back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Can you now please proceed with what happened next in the afternoon of the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 14.44 hours, I had another conversation with Franjo Nakic. I asked him what happened to the kidnapped officers of the Subic-Zrinjski Brigade command staff and with Commander Totic, and Nakic informed me that they, meaning the kidnapped officers, were in the barracks of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where was Nakic at that time?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, Nakic was at his family home.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where did he live at that time?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He lived in the village of Zabrdje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Continue from there.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 14.46, I called the main headquarters of the HVO and informed them about the agreement on cessation of combat operations and let them know that we were working on calming down the situation and that we had been promised that the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was also going to issue orders on cessation of all further combat operations. I also informed the main staff that at that time Vitez was still being shelled from a tank of the BH army from the Preocica Samar feature. A bit later on, at 14.50, Mr. Pilicic called UNPROFOR regarding the evacuation of wounded in Poculica, and at that time he was given a promise that this evacuation would be carried out by UNPROFOR. At 14.57 -- yes, at 14.57, we conducted a check, that is, a correction together with the artillery battery. That was a correction of the artillery fire. At 15.00 hours, I received information from Commander Cerkez that a conversation between the commander of the BH army had been taped and that from this tape we could conclude that the BH army is moving from Zenica in the direction of Vitez. Following this information, I called the commander in Zenica, Mr. Baresic, and inquired about what he knew about the movements of the BH army from Zenica. Commander Baresic informed me that he still did not have such information but that he would check on it. At 15.08, a report from Mario Cerkez arrived, number 02-125-13/93 of 16 April, 1993, at 14.50 hours. On the basis of this report, I called Cerkez and ordered him to hold and reinforce the positions which he currently held. At 15.10, I had further communication with the commander of the combined artillery battery and further correction of artillery fire. At 15.15, I sent a written report to the main headquarters of the HVO in Mostar and to the headquarters of the North-western Herzegovina Operative Zone in Tomislavgrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: By what method did you send this report?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This report was sent by packet communication network. At 15.22, I was informed that no subordinate unit from the Central Bosnia Operative Zone had any secret code names so that it was not possible to have communication in a secure way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Secret code names. If you used those, what method of communication would you use if you had those names?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If we had secret code names, then we could have communicated by radio and even by telephone, but then we would not call each other by first and last names or by your position in the command structure, that every commander would have his code name by which he would be addressed. Also, in any combat activities, just as you make a plan of artillery fire, you also compile a similar plan of communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is it a regular thing to make such a plan in the middle of a battle?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Such a document is always drafted ahead of time, that is, before the start of combat activities and is usually part of the preparatory organisational documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 15.26, a report was sent for -- public information was released, and at 15.31, I had contact with the commander of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade, Mr. Grubesic, and I asked him to hold the positions at Kuber at any cost and to endeavour to regain the positions which he had lost in the course of the day. I believe that those positions were Obla Glava and Vrana Stijene.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So he had lost those positions in the course of the day?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. They had been pushed back from those positions during the course of the day, that is, the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 15.40, I called Mr. Samija, the chief of the civilian police in Vitez, in order to get an update on the security situation in the town of Vitez. I did not get him at that time, but at 15.42 hours, Samija called me and informed me that security in the town of Vitez at that point in time was under control, and I requested that he identify the positions from which BH army snipers were active and from which positions they were shooting at the Operative Zone command headquarters, that is, the Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, who was in charge of the security for the town of Vitez in combat conditions?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was the competence of the civilian police authority in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you receive any kind of information from the civilian police authorities whether any kind of violence was being committed against civilians?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I took down and I wrote down all information that I received in the course of that day, and I received no such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 15.50, I called the commander of the Vitez Brigade, Mr. Mario Cerkez, and asked for information about the situation in the village of Donja Veceriska. He informed me that the situation in Donja Veceriska was still critical. At 15.51, Slavko Marin talked to the commander of the combined artillery battery regarding correction of fire. I also received information on firing of our artillery on our targets, in other words, the HVO artillery was shelling our own positions. Dario Kordic transmitted this information to me, and following that, I checked the coordinates and I determined at 15.54 that the artillery of the BH army was shelling our positions or firing on our positions and that this fire was not coming from the HVO artillery on the HVO positions. At 16.00 hours, I talked to the commander in Travnik, Mr. Filip Filipovic, and inquired about the situation in the town of Travnik, and he told me that the situation was calm for the time being. I also had a conversation around 16.00 hours with the commander from Kiseljak, Mr. Mijo Bozic, who informed me that the situation was calm, and I told him that for the time being, we were holding out, considering primarily the situation in Busovaca and Vitez. Then I had contact at 16.10 with Dr. Dzambas from the Franciscan hospital in Nova Bila who reported on the number of wounded they received and the situation in the hospital. At 16.15, I asked the commander of the artillery battery to report on the levels of ammunition with the artillery battery. At 16.18, I had a conversation with a commander who introduced himself by his nickname, which was Munja. He was with the 2nd Corps of the BH army which was headquartered in Tuzla. He transmitted information that he had personally talked to Brigadier Petkovic and that he had mediated in order to achieve a cease-fire, and he said that he personally was doing everything in his power in order to achieve a truce and cease-fire. At 16.47, I once again talked to the commander of the Vitez Brigade, Mr. Mario Cerkez, and the questions were the situation in the town with regard to Stari Vitez. Cerkez informed me that they lacked materiel, that they lacked barrels, rifle barrels, for the recruits, and also that they lacked ammunition, and that they had a great deal of difficulty because of sniper fire and the effects of devices in Stari Vitez, machine guns from Stari Vitez. I told him that he should organise his defence with what he had available at that time. I had in mind resources, materiel, and weapons. At 17.08, Mr. Tuka called, the commander of the HVO Battalion in Fojnica, and he was interested in knowing what the situation was like in Vitez and Busovaca. He informed me that the situation in Fojnica was fairly tense but that there were no actual conflicts in Fojnica at that particular time. At 17.11, I tried to contact the main staff, and at 17.15, I managed to contact the main staff and told them that the situation had calmed down and that some of the roads, and I had in mind the main roads from Busovaca to Vitez and further on towards Travnik, that that main road was under the control of the BH army whereas part of the roads were under the control of the Croatian Defence Council. I also informed the main staff that we still did not have any information as to what had actually happened to the kidnapped officers, Zivko Totic and the four officers from the Stejpan Tomasevic Brigade of Novi Travnik, apart from the fact that we knew that they were being held in the barracks of the 7th Muslim Brigade according to information that I was conveyed from the chief of staff. I also stressed that I assumed that the resources being used to fight us, to attack us, were probably taken from the convoy intended for eastern Bosnia between the 11th and 12th of April, 1993. After that, Petkovic, Commander Petkovic, said, "Don't believe in the cease-fire alone but start fortifying yourselves."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does that mean? What kind of activity is fortification? What does that imply?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It implied that at the positions we held, that we undertake the engineering type of fortification for the terrain to defend. This is a defence activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mentioned control of roads. It's not quite clear, according to the interpretation, who was controlling which roads.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I conveyed the information that part of the roads -- and I'm thinking of the entire zone, all the roads in the zone, of the Operative Zone -- that we were in control of them whereas one portion of the roads were under the control of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Petkovic, the chief of the main staff, told me that manpower had been mobilised in Kiseljak and in Fojnica to the full and that it should be on the ready. At about 17.41, I talked to Darko Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was that your first conversation on that particular day with Darko Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was my first conversation with Darko Kraljevic on the 16th of April, on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What did he inform you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He informed me of the action coming from Stari Vitez, and I asked him to wait, not to go forward, and to keep the positions held under control, all the directions of combat activity from Stari Vitez towards the headquarters and towards the town of Vitez, and especially to bear in mind the civilians because we assumed that the civilians themselves could start moving out of Stari Vitez in the direction of Vitez town, and I particularly drew his attention to the fact that he should not just move forward but should bear in mind the civilians and look after the women and children.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, I suggest that we take a 30-minute break, and we will resume at noon and continue until 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now resume the hearing. Mr. Nobilo and Mr. Hayman, think about keeping five or six minutes before the end of the hearing so you can give us an evaluation about the time that you're going to need. I will ask the registrar how much time has already been used for this testimony, the testimony of General Blaskic. We can ask him at that point. All right. Let's resume now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I think we left off somewhere around 17.48 hours onwards. What happened after that, after you warned Kraljevic not to touch the civilians and the women and children?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I received a report on the casualties from the Vitez Brigade, the facts that they had collected up until then. There were six killed members of the Vitez Brigade and a number of members who were injured, lightly injured. At 17.48, I also asked the commander of the mixed artillery division to remain in a state of alert. At 17.55, I received a report from the military intelligence service that the BH army units were asking for assistance in the areas of Vranjska and Kruscica and that there were problems there. I received information from the Vitezovi that three Vitezovi members had been killed, one civilian, and two other casualties, I don't know exactly where those casualties were, but that meant a total of six dead. At 18.02, I received information from Mr. Kordic who told me that Pasko's people were going up the hill and that he had done his part and that he had intercepted a telegram about panic in their ranks, and at 18.04, I called the commander of the mixed artillery battalion to prepare to fire along the 649 feature, the 649 position or feature. At 18.07, I talked to Mr. Mario Cerkez, the commander of the Vitez Brigade, and asked him to reinforce security around the explosives factory and that he take care of the Kruscica and Vranjska situation. At 18.10, I received a call from Bugojno, and they were interested in knowing about the situation and state of affairs in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, and we sent them information about that. At 18.25, Cerkez asked for assistance, to have auxiliary logistics supplies, for resupplies. At 18.29, I had a conversation with the commander of the Operative Zone of Northwest Herzegovina, Mr. Zeljko Siljeg, and I told him, "Convey to your chief that everything has been sent to me, going through me, and that he should bear this in mind and extend assistance."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who was the chief? Your terminology, the one you used, who was the chief you referred to?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The chief was, in fact, the head of the main staff of the HVO. At 18.32, I asked reconnoitring of the points of impact in the Vranjska area by the commander of the mixed artillery battalion --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before we continue, can we add a little more clarification on your talks about Siljeg? When you said "everything is turned towards me," what did you mean by that because in the interpretation, it was "sent to me" or "turned towards me." You said that everything was turned towards you. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I thought that the bulk of the forces of the 3rd Corps were being directed towards Vitez and part of Busovaca, that is to say, that there was movement present, a regrouping of troops and combat operations in the area of Vitez and Busovaca, and when I said "everything," I meant all mobile forces at that time were looking towards me and towards the defenders of the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you told Siljeg to convey to Petkovic that he should help, how did Petkovic, from Mostar, how was he able to help you in that kind of situation? What did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In that kind of situation, Petkovic could -- the only effective way of helping us was to call the head of the main staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Sefer Halilovic, and to work with him towards a cease-fire agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In the course of the day, you had already issued an order for a cease-fire. What information did you get from the ground in all the reports coming in to you? Was this being implemented? If not, why not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is true that I issued an order for a cease-fire, but this order was probably not received by the units of the 3rd Corps because combat operations continued. There was a continued regrouping of forces, and fresh troops were being brought in so that, according to the reports that I received, it was not possible to establish and implement a cease-fire at that particular time, a truce.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who brought in fresh troops?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us continue and look at the events after 18.50 hours onwards.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 18.50, I had a telephone conversation with Dario Kordic, and he informed me that he had received information from Zenica about the movement of 350 to 400 soldiers towards Kuber, soldiers of the BH army moving towards Kuber. I once again contacted, at 18.51 or 18.52, immediately after that, the commander of the mixed artillery battalion and asked them to be placed on the ready, to open fire in the direction of Kuber. At 18.58, I asked that preparations in the MTD be speeded up with regard to combat readiness. At 19.06, there was a momentary interruption of communications with the command of the Zenica Brigade, and I was not able to contact Vinko Baresic at that particular time, and at 19.08, I phoned the commander of MTD once again because the preparations had not been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: "MTD," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
