utterances.text: It was the mixed artillery battalion, the commander of the mixed artillery battalion, MTD. At 19.10 or 19.11 hours, I talked to Commander Baresic from Zenica and checked with him the information that I had received about the movement of troops of the BH army from Zenica towards Kuber, and I asked him that this movement of troops be stopped so that, if necessary, he ought to deploy all the manpower that he had at his disposal to achieve that goal. At about 19.12, I sent, via my associates, a request to the defence department of the Vitez municipality asking them to mobilise manpower for the shifts. At 19 --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What kind of shifts? What were these shifts?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was a question of mobilising recruits who were to replace, in the course of the night, recruits who had already been engaged in the fighting in the course of the day. At 19.14, I received a request from the mixed artillery battalion asking me whether they should still direct their attention towards Kuber, and I answered in the affirmative, I said yes. At 19.15, a report was drafted for the public, a public statement, and I also received information once again that, from Zenica, there were troop movements on the part of the BH army towards Vitez at 19.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me. General Blaskic, you say that it was a statement that had been drafted, but very, very quickly, can you tell us what was in it? We don't have the proof. We don't have the documents. You said that there was a public statement that had been drafted, that's fine, but what's in it? Otherwise, we've got a catalogue of all the things that you did all day long, but I think that what's interesting is in respect of what can be brought back to the accusations of the Prosecutor. What did it say? Were you being attacked? Were you being placed under siege? It will only take you a minute to tell us. Do you understand what I'm looking for, what I mean?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, not completely. I don't understand your thoughts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps I didn't explain myself cleverly. You're giving a very detailed description of your schedule, but at some point, you have to tell us whether it's only on the basis of your memory or on military logs, but that's another question, and we can ask that at another time, but there are certain facts about all you say is the fact itself. For example, at 10.15, there was a public statement which had been drafted. I have to say to you, "Well, yes, all right, but what was said in the public statement?" There's no point in reading it, there's no point in providing us with it, but what was the general sense of that public statement, that is, your statement or the statement of the municipal authorities? Do you understand what I mean?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, Mr. President. The notes are notes that were made at the time, that is to say, when the events took place, and I said at the beginning of my testimony that I had asked an associate of mine to write down everything he heard and saw going on in the hall where there were only seven of us on that particular day, the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are these your assistant's notes, the notes that you're using?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. In preparing, that is to say, when I decided to come to this Tribunal, I used all available documents at that time. When I say "that time," I have in mind 1995, it was November and December of 1995, and I did this, Mr. President, in such a way that I wrote down the chronology, copying from those notes, and on the basis of my own notes, the notes that I made then, I was able to write my first written statement. For this testimony, I just have an agenda and perhaps the name of the person who telephoned me and briefly the contents of that telephone conversation, so these are notes to remind me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Therefore, to go back to the example, that was the reason I interrupted you, and I apologise again for having done so, at 10.15, there was a public statement which was drafted, and that means that you no longer remember what was in the statement.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At this point in time, I cannot reproduce the contents of that public statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. You've explained it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps it would be a good idea if the witness were to tell us when he no longer remembers the details but just has copied a fact from a document and one of the notes so that you know when he remembers the details himself and when he doesn't actually remember himself because, of course, six years have gone by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: When the time is appropriate, and you are the one to decide when that is, you can mention, for example, "There is a public statement but I don't remember its contents." For instance, if you don't remember, you just tell us. All right? Please continue. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We stopped at 19.15 and the public statement, and after that, you had Zenica on the line and received information on new troop movements of the BH army. That was the last thing you said.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Once again, I contacted the commander from Zenica and received information about troop movements, and at 19.25, I had a telephone conversation with Mr. Dario Kordic who conveyed the same piece of information to me, namely, that BH army movements from Zenica were under way from Zenica towards Kuber and that we could expect the main onslaught to take place on that section. At about 19.30, I called the chief of the main staff in Mostar and informed him of this regrouping of forces which was taking place from the direction of Zenica towards Vitez, and I asked him once again, asked the chief of the main staff once again, to get in contact with the competent authorities in the BH army and to attempt to settle the problem of this influx of reinforcements, and I relied on this, on the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What agreement?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I told the chief of the main staff that while some individuals were negotiating with us, others were attacking us, and I had in mind the agreement of the 16th of April, 1993, that had been reached in Vitez at the UNPROFOR base there. I also emphasised that the -- I informed the chief of the main staff that most of the activity was from the direction of Zenica towards Vitez, and I reported to him about the state of affairs in the village of Poculica where the Croats had all been taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you talk about whether the Bosnian side was disseminating propaganda that a mosque had been demolished somewhere? Do you recall that during your conversation with General Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I do not recall that right now. But at 19.35 hours, I was informed that members of the combined artillery battalion had carried out their task. At 19.40, I issued an order for withdrawal of a military police unit from Travnik to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How was this carried out and what was the purpose of it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The purpose of it was to introduce a new shift of manpower at these positions and that this new shift would fortify the positions in the course of the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On whose request did you carry this order out?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: These men were supposed to report to me at the hotel, and the military police, actually the commander, Pasko, of the military police, sent me this request.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know why he did not do this on his own but asked that this be done through your office?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was a military police unit which had earlier been sent to Travnik, and I don't know whether at that time he had communication with them from the position where he was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So am I correct in concluding that you did this on request of Mr. Ljubicic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He requested that I write such an order, that his men be brought back to Vitez so that he could have a shift for the men which he already had deployed and who were fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 19.45, I again received a call from Commander Mario Cerkez asking for assistance from the Busovaca Brigade and asking me to mediate in providing this assistance. I also, at 19.45, talked to Pasko, and asked him to start digging in and develop the defence further.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is Pasko Ljubicic, commander of the military police?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why, at that point in time, did you order him to dig in? What was the reason for it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had received information that his position was on the high ground, that is, on the slope of Barin Gaj and Kratine, and I believed that it was necessary to fortify this position and prepare for defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is what you thought, but today, having heard everything that has been testified to in the Tribunal, was he up there in the high ground or was that incorrect information?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I acted based on what he told me, but I believe that he was never at Barin Gaj because the HVO never held this position at Barin Gaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you issued this order because you did not have the right information about this position?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 19.50, I had another conversation with the commander of the Vitez Brigade, Mario Cerkez, and I asked that he start fortifying himself and get ready for the shift of his men at his position, in other words, to organise a shift at his position. At 19.55, I received a call from the commander of the Travnik Brigade, Filipovic, and he informed me that the roads via Han Bila and Ovnak were closed for any kind of traffic. Filipovic also inquired about the situation in Vitez and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Exhibit D281, Defence Exhibit D281, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is the Defence Exhibit D281 and is an order which you issued to the Busovaca Brigade on 16 April, 1993, at 19.45. I will only read the first point. It is a combat order for the defence of Kuber. "1. Extremist Muslim forces are advancing from the direction of Gornja Zenica toward Kuber with the objective of completely capturing it and cutting it off." And then you task the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade further. Is this the order you just referred to?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Perhaps you could help us to clarify what is in the upper right corner. Something is written in handwriting.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is a warning for --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please read this again?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me read it one more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In the upper right corner, in handwriting, a sentence was added, and it reads as follows. Let us put it on the ELMO. Somebody added this in handwriting and it reads as follows: "An oral advisement for the implementation and reporting on the combat orders received," and there is somebody's either initial or signature. Could you decipher who wrote this and who signed it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the signature, it is Slavko Marin's signature, and this advisement, I remember this, referred to the full implementation and detailed report on the combat order which had been issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, is this a regular procedure, that a subordinate commander has to remind field commanders that they had to implement orders or carry them out?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Whenever you have a well-trained and organised army, this would not be necessary, to specially emphasise such things, because it is something that is implicit in the order. But I was concerned, given the overall situation, and I tried to have as complete information as was possible about a given situation, and with respect to this order, as you see, we were still insisting on the defence of Kuber, and it is not clear who was holding which position at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This remark, does it show that the orders were not carried out completely and that you did not have full control of the situation? Is that the significance of the oral advisements?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is its significance, but also the fact that we were trying to get full information and that we tried to have the orders implemented in full and as they were issued or written.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us move on, follow the chronology of events.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Around 19.55, a request to the defence department to carry out an additional mobilisation of the available manpower because we had received information that the previous requests were not honoured, and I'm referring here to the previous calls for mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So was this an alarming situation or was this a regular situation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I talked to the chief of the defence administration because we were lacking in manpower, and I asked him to become involved and to mobilise whoever can carry a gun, even up to the age of 70, if there were still military recruits, because we had a severe shortage of manpower.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Again, based on your training and experience, is it a normal thing to carry out mobilisation at the end of the first day of a war?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That would depend upon the size of the unit, but you would need at least 48 hours before the start of combat operations; in other words, you need that period of time for preparation in order to be able to start combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So why didn't you carry out mobilisation before the beginning of war?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We did not expect conflicts of this magnitude, and in the latter part of March, I was giving away supplies and ordinance for the 3rd Corps, and Mr. Prskalo, when he returned from negotiations, this is what the army is doing. They are returning the ordinance which we had given them, only they are sending them through the barrels.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I understand he was a bit sarcastic here. But let us move on with the chronology of events.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 20.22, I again talked to Commander Baresic from Zenica, and I requested that he check on any troop movements from Zenica in the direction of Vitez and to halt the forces that may be moving from Zenica in the direction of Vitez. At 20.45, I received information from Mr. Dario Kordic that the following day a meeting would probably be organised in Zenica with Dzemo Merdan and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Sometime after 20.00 hours, 20.25, together with Jozo Lozancic, you conducted a military manoeuvre which was supposed to fool the enemy?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, I asked Lozancic and I told him that he was going to receive a document. In this document, I explained that it was necessary that he was to fake that he was preparing an attack on Zenica. I informed him that my communication with him would be in the sense that it would have to do with the regrouping and bringing fresh forces from Zenica to Vitez, but I knew that our telephone conversations were being monitored, so in the spirit of that, I would ask Lozancic whether the forces were ready in Zepce even though at that time there were absolutely no troop movements in Zepce on the part of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was the meaning of it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The objective was to slow down the arrival of troops in Vitez and basically our survival in Vitez because I was afraid that the vast majority of the 3rd Corps troops would move in on the positions of the HVO against the Operative Zone command and create further enclaves; in other words, I wanted to alleviate the situation of the HVO positions in the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 21.02, Pasko came to me, Pasko Ljubicic, the commander of the 4th Military Police Battalion, and he informed me that he needed urgently to replace the shift, and I agreed with him that as we had not had fresh troops, as we didn't have fresh troops, that he should take the entire staff from the Vitez Hotel and take them with him to effect this changing of shifts. So that sometime from 21.00 onwards or 21.02, the headquarters were left without any military policemen who were otherwise engaged to secure the hotel, provide security for the hotel. I had expected the unit that I had ordered from Travnik, that it might possibly arrive sometime in the course of the night, the military police unit, and that it would be able to take over the security of the hotel and the headquarters of the Operative Zone. This fresh manpower would probably be engaged by Pasko to take over the shift and to dig in the positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before Pasko asked you to supply him with fresh forces for the shift, can you remember whether he came personally or phoned? Do you remember that? If not, we can move on. Do you remember a report to the 3rd Corps and a written report to the main HVO command?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: A report to the 3rd Corps was sent at about 21.00, and it referred to the lack of respect for the truce. It was a notice that we sent. This written notice to the main staff was also sent, but it was sent at 20.45. I have a note here saying that at 20.15, I ordered the commander of the mixed artillery battalion to ensure that firing positions were secured for the mixed artillery battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please proceed according to your chronology of events.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 21.20, I received a report saying that in the course of the night, the military police unit from Travnik would not be transported to Vitez. At 21.50 hours, I was called up by Mr. Nikola Krizanovic, he was the director of the explosives factory, and he informed me that there was strong shooting in the immediate vicinity of the explosives factory. At 23.50, I had a conversation with the deputy chief of civilian police of the Vitez police station, Mr. Slavko Jukic, and I asked him to extend assistance to us in order to ensure security for the hotel and the headquarters of the Operative Zone from the direction of Stari Vitez whereas -- in the course of that night and the next day until the military police from Travnik were able to arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This completes our chronology of events for the 16th of April, and we should now like to focus on some important documents that you received in written form and are not included in your chronology. I should like the witness now to be handed Defence Exhibit D280.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic, the Judges are prepared to allow you to withdraw for a few moments if you feel tired so that you can rest for five minutes. Would you care to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would welcome that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We can resume the hearing now. General Blaskic, do you feel better? Do you feel better? Are you all right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President. I wasn't tuned in to the channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I just wanted to know if you were all right, if you were feeling okay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. President. I feel much better. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So do we. Okay. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before the recess, D280 was handed round, and I'm going to briefly read this very important report. The commander of the military police, Pasko Ljubicic, was writing to you on the 16th of April, 1993, and he says: "Acting in accordance with your order number 01-04-243/93 of the 16th of April, 1993, we hereby report: Muslim armed forces attempted to launch, in the early hours of the morning, an attack on the military police units located in the Bungalow. The attack met with response, and combat procedures and actions were undertaken to expel the same. Muslim armed forces barricaded themselves in a mosque in Ahmici and in the primary school from where they have been firing from small arms weapons and snipers. They have been opening light fire from the direction of the villages of Vrhovine and Pirici, and snipers have been constantly firing from the woods and clearings above the village. So far three policemen have been killed and three were wounded, one of whom seriously. Personnel is in the field." The stamp is the command of the military police in Mostar, and it says, "Commander Pasko Ljubicic." Tell us now, what was the order of the 16th of April that was issued to Pasko Ljubicic, chief of military police, by you and why?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was an order to report to me in writing regarding the situation in the field because reports and information from the chief of the military police I generally received via telephone and orally, and he did not send reports in written form, in writing, as was done by the commander of the Vitez Brigade and the commander of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade. He did not send them to me. As the fighting had already started, I considered that it was necessary to caution him that, in future, he should send me reports as my immediate subordinates did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was your legal basis, military legal basis, for asking the chief of the military police, as you did from your own commanders, to ask him to send you written reports?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Subordination or attachment, the attachment of the military police unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would you remind us what this term "attachment of units" implies and "subordination of units" implies?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It means that during the implementation of assignment, a higher command for a certain unit can be placed within the composition of a lower command, be attached to it for performing certain assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does that mean that Pasko Ljubicic, as the chief of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Counsel. I think the proper question is "What does it mean?" and not telling the witness what it means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Nobilo. I think that we've said many things about the testimony. The Judges have expressed their opinion, they've said that they don't agree with the way it's being conducted, and you know, Mr. Kehoe, you always have to show some degree of flexibility, but we're being very vigilant here. As soon as Mr. Nobilo takes the place of the witness, we're going to interrupt him, but that's not what's happened here. Continue, Mr. Nobilo, but don't make too many suggestions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me remember what it was that I was asking, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, was the military police subordinate to you or attached to you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the basis of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Once again, problems with interpretation. Let me repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The military police, in the battle of the 16th of April, was it attached to you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was attached to me. Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. President, that certainly was not the question that was initially asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Well, let's talk to the interpreter's booth about that, Mr. President. Let's ask them and let's let them tell us what the question was, whether they were correcting themselves or whether Mr. Nobilo corrected himself. Let's ask them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You're going too fast because I haven't heard the end of the interpretation of the first question, and already things are coming out from all sides. Let's stay calm, please. Mr. Kehoe, what is your objection? Let me hear the objection, and then I promise you, Mr. Hayman, I will listen to you immediately after that. What is your objection, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My comment is simply this, Mr. President, that one question was asked and then another question was asked according to the interpretation. Mr. Hayman maintains that the problem was, in fact, with the interpretation, which I find somewhat astonishing since he doesn't speak the language. Nevertheless, the question, it seems, coming from the interpreters at the outset was quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let's ask them, Mr. President. Let's ask them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a moment. Mr. Hayman, Mr. Hayman, first I'd like to hear what your objection is. What is your objection? What is it? You don't agree with Mr. Kehoe; I think that's what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe is attempting to create doubt in Your Honours' minds as to the words or phrases used by Mr. Nobilo to suggest that Mr. Nobilo thinks that the military police were subordinate to then Colonel Blaskic on the 16th, and we commented on the same situation one or two days ago with respect to the interpreting booth correcting themselves with respect to a translation. I understand they spoke to Your Honours after that incident, and they told you that, in fact, they were correcting themselves, they were not correcting Mr. -- I believe in that instance, it was not Mr. Nobilo, it was the accused, with respect to very important matters of phraseology. Once again, Mr. Kehoe is suggesting that Mr. Nobilo has performed some sleight of hand to switch the words "subordination" and "assignment" -- excuse me, "attached." I would ask Your Honours, please, we don't want any ambiguity or doubt in the record of this case. Let's ask the interpreter booth whether Mr. Nobilo used those terms interchangeably in his question or did they correct themselves and, in fact, Mr. Nobilo used the term "attached" and did not use the term "subordinated to."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, thank you. We certainly want to hear what you have to say, and you are an extraordinary champion for Mr. Nobilo, as well as an excellent and fervent Defence attorney for Mr. Blaskic. If you had allowed me to finish, I would have said that I did not agree with Mr. Kehoe. I had understood that this was not an assertion by Mr. Nobilo but that, at least in the interpretation that I heard, it was simply that he was asking the accused whether the military police were subordinate to him at that point, pursuant to what order. That was your question, was it not, Mr. Hayman, or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Not in the English, not in the English, Mr. President, no, that was not the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That's very simple. It's fourteen minutes after one, I'll do like the accused, at fourteen after one, the Presiding Judge is asking Mr. Nobilo to ask his question again; at quarter after one, Mr. Nobilo answered, and 30 seconds after that, the English interpreters were asked to interpret Mr. Nobilo's question correctly, and that will be the end of the incident. Mr. Nobilo, please speak slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question in a neutral way so that it will be perfectly clear and the response be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The question, General, is what was your relationship towards the military police on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, 1993, when the fighting started, I was superior to the military police, in a position of superiority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think you asked a different question. You asked pursuant to what order, on what basis that had happened. That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me just try to further specify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was the legal basis so that they were in such a position in relation to you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The legal basis was the order of the chief of the main headquarters on the 15th of April, 1993 and the start of the combat operations in the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the military police become permanently subordinated to you at that point or just for the duration of the combat?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Only for the duration of the combat activities. It did not change its structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was that the same basis under which the Vitezovi were involved in fighting?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That was from the 15th of April; is that the date of the order? Mr. Nobilo, it was the order from General Petkovic dated the 15th of April; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: As far as I understood, this was the order on the attachment of the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Have you finished with the 16th of April, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No. We have some documents. We are finished in terms of the chronology, but if we can just finish with this report from Ahmici, then we can break off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next question: According to the overall full information which we have received to date, was this report accurate or did it mislead you? Did they mislead you about what had happened in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This report on the events in Ahmici was not accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Apart from this report and oral reports which you have mentioned today which you received from Pasko Ljubicic, did you have any other knowledge about what was happening in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I received information from Pasko Ljubicic by telephone, and, in addition, I received this written report. I had no other information on the events there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have now finished with this report from Ahmici, and if you feel that we should not go into additional documents, we can break off here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like two clarifications. I didn't understand this and perhaps it was an interpretation problem. I turn both to the accused and to the Defence. You say that the report is from Pasko Ljubicic and that it was not exact, was not precise. Have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. He said that now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Why was it not accurate? In what way was it not accurate? Do you understand that? In what way was it not? We are speaking about this report that I've shown my colleagues dated the 16th of April and that we read a little while back, saying that the HOS had barricaded themselves at the Ahmici mosque. Where is it incorrect? I think it's on the ELMO. I think the English version is on the ELMO, and the registrar has given it to me in French. In what way was it not precise?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, as far as I recall, the question was whether this report reflected the actual military situation in Ahmici, and based on subsequent knowledge and information I have had since, I can say that, no, it was not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me ask you this question: Based on what you know today, who attacked whom in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Based on what I know now, today, the military police attacked units of the BH army and villagers of Ahmici, that is, Bosniak Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So this was the military police under your orders. Otherwise, I don't understand. That is what you said, is it not? According to what you know today -- no, that's not right? Mr. Nobilo is saying "Yes" and -- Mr. Nobilo is saying "Yes" and Mr. Hayman is saying "No." All right. For the time being, we won't go any further. Before we move to another subject, with respect to the report, the order from the chief of the headquarters dated 15 April, who attached the military police to the Vitezovi; was it tendered as evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We do not have this order because this was an internal correspondence between the military police and the Vitezovi, and as you can see, we have practically no documents which were produced by the military police, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, did you wish to say something before we moved to another subject?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just this, Mr. President: Categorically, no, that has not been introduced into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Okay. I think that we said we would stop a little before the end of the time, that is, at the beginning of the 17th of April. Before we go our separate ways, I would like to turn to Mr. Dubuisson and ask him where we are. I think you gave me the numbers here with respect to the hours that we have spent here, but could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The examination-in-chief of the accused to date, since Wednesday, 17th February, which was the first day of the examination-in-chief of the accused, there have been 29 hours and 5 minutes, that is, five and a half hearing days out of a total of eight calendar days. There was one -- I remind that one hearing day is five hours and twenty minutes of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps the Defence could tell us -- I think originally we spoke about 35 hours. I'm sure it's going to take more than another six hours. But could you give us an evaluation of the time, because what you tell us is going to have an effect on the cross-examination. Could you give us an evaluation, Mr. Hayman, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Gladly, Mr. President. We estimate that yesterday afternoon, when we finished the 15th of April, which was roughly in the middle of the afternoon yesterday, we were at approximately the halfway point in the direct examination. If we take the amount of time -- and I just did a rough calculation measuring days, not hours -- if we take how long it took us to get to yesterday at 3.00 and we double it in terms of the court schedule that I understand we have, that will take us to approximately the end of the first week of our next trial session, which is the 12th of March, 1999, for the completion of the direct examination. I note that is not a scientific estimate; it is our best estimate. I think the Court should assume plus or minus one day equivalent, perhaps, for planning purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We will let Mr. Dubuisson do the calculations. So that takes us to the 12th of March. Looking at the schedule, we are not sitting next week; therefore, we will sit again the week of the 8th to the 12th; is that correct? So we will begin at 2.00 on the 8th and we will continue until the 12th. So you think that by Friday, 12 March, you will most likely be finished?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That is our best estimate, plus or minus one trial day equivalent, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Does this allow the Office of the Prosecutor to know about how much time it is going to need?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's, of course, an estimate, Your Honour. Of course, that gives us an idea --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, it gives you an idea. But the Judges, at the proper time, will tell you that you will have the same amount of time for the cross-examination as for the direct examination, so you can select your questions. Try to show some degree of flexibility, but you will have more or less the same time, the same amount of time. If you know in advance, you can organise yourselves accordingly. That also depends upon the length of the answers. But the principle is that you will have the same amount of time as was spent during the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We just should say good-bye now to one another. We won't see each other next week, but we will see one another on the week of the 8th of March. Is that not correct, Mr. Dubuisson? All right. Court stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
